subject: Developer handoff: LotusPay SDK onboarding and endpoint migration
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lotuspay.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: LotusPay -> Redwood handoff + MAP (SDK focus)

Kim, Marissa —

Quick handoff: LotusPay (Samira) is ready to move from evaluation to pilot. They want an SDK-first integration (Node + Python), need a migration plan from their current hosted endpoint to our dedicated endpoint later in the quarter, and are sensitive to retry behavior (they have bursty traffic from payment reconciliation jobs).

I've attached the mutual action plan and a zip with baseline SDK samples we used in the POC. High-level asks from the call:
- Confirm recommended initial config for SDK (timeouts, default retry/backoff).
- Provide a staged endpoint migration checklist (hosted->dedicated).
- Notes on rate-limit handling for their reconciliation bursts.

Samira, looping you in — Kimberly will lead onboarding and Marissa will be the technical AE for the pilot.

Next step: Kimberly, can you propose a 2-week implementation runway with checkpoints?

Thanks,
Ben
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20280621_LotusPay_mutual_action_plan.xlsx, redwood_sdk_examples_v1.zip

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lotuspay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LotusPay -> Redwood handoff + MAP (SDK focus)

Hi Samira — nice to meet you (virtually). Thanks Ben for the intro and the materials.

Samira, I put together a compact 2-week onboarding runway tailored to an SDK-led integration. Summary below; full MAP attached.

Week 1 (Discovery & dev sandbox)
- Day 1: Kickoff call (30 min) to align integration owner and deliverables.
- Day 2-4: Access + credentials: dev API key, sandbox dedicated endpoint, and sample dataset.
- Day 5-7: SDK quickstart (Node + Python): basic generate/embed calls + local tests.

Week 2 (Stability & migration planning)
- Day 8-11: Retry/backoff and rate-limit tuning: run load test with reconciliation pattern; we’ll provide recommended config.
- Day 12: Endpoint migration checklist review (hosted -> dedicated staging).
- Day 13-14: Go/no-go for pilot; schedule cutover window.

Quick notes on the technical items you asked about (expanded in the attached runbook):
- SDK defaults: 5s connect timeout, 30s request timeout, max retries 4 (with jittered exponential backoff).
- Retry semantics: idempotent vs non-idempotent guidance included; prefer per-call idempotency tokens for reconciliation jobs.
- Rate limits: per-account token bucket on hosted; dedicated pools will give you guaranteed throughput — we’ll provide per-minute quota numbers once capacity is reserved.

Can you confirm the best time for the kickoff (we have availability tomorrow 10–12 PDT or Thursday 14–16 PDT)?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: LotusPay_onboarding_runbook_v1.pdf (see MAP for milestones)

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lotuspay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LotusPay -> Redwood handoff + MAP (SDK focus)

Thanks Kimberly — Thursday 14:00 PDT works. A couple of clarifying questions in advance so our engineers can prep:

1) SDK support: Are the SDKs distributed via npm/pypi and pinned to semver? Do you provide shrinkwrapped examples or Docker images?
2) Endpoint migration: what is the recommended approach to migrate API keys and maintain in-flight job continuity?
3) Rate-limit behavior: during the POC we saw '429' spikes when 1000 small reconciliation calls queued. Is there guidance to smooth this without increasing request latency?

We will have two engineers on the call: Rajesh (backend) and Elena (integration).

—Samira
Head of Integrations, LotusPay

> Hi Samira, Rajesh, Elena —
> 
> Good questions. Short answers and attached examples. Full notes in the runbook attachment; below is a condensed actionable checklist you can hand to your engineers.

Thanks Kimberly — that Node sample is exactly what we needed. A few follow-ups from our engineer:

1) In the sample you use process.env.REDWOOD_ENDPOINT — will the hosted endpoint still return the x-rw-limit-* headers, or are those only on dedicated pools?
2) For mirroring to dedicated during Phase A, do you have a recommended validation script? We’d like an end-to-end checksum on a subset of transactions.

We can run the validation script during our staging window on Monday.

—Rajesh
Senior Backend Engineer, LotusPay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: LotusPay -> Redwood handoff + MAP (SDK focus) — validation script + next steps

Rajesh —

Quick answers:
1) Hosted endpoints do return x-rw-limit-* headers; dedicated adds per-pool capacity headers as well (we'll include exact header examples in the runbook).
2) Attached: validation.sh — a small script that posts a 100-item sample payload to both endpoints and compares hashes of the responses. It uses the idempotency key we recommend.

I pushed validation.sh to the shared Drive folder (link above). If you run it in staging and paste the results in this thread we’ll review together Monday.

Kimberly — I’ll join the kickoff to walk through the validation step and help tune the leaky-bucket config during the load run.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Technical Account Executive
Redwood Inference
